findings.rule: Full depth — hip below top of patella
findings.source_quote: Correctly is deep, with hips dropping below level with the top of the patellas
findings.feedback: Reached full depth: the hip crease apex was 26 px below the top of the patella at the bottom of the rep (reference p2).

findings.rule: Back angle — torso inclined, not vertical
findings.source_quote: the back is at an angle (about 45 degrees) that will place the bar over the middle of the foot
findings.feedback: Back angle of 57 degrees is consistent with the inclined torso the document describes for the low-bar squat (about 45 degrees, reference p22).

findings.rule: Hip and knee angles (diagnostic, observation only)
findings.source_quote: The hip angle is formed by the plane of the torso and the femur. The knee angle is formed by the femur and the tibia
findings.feedback: Hip angle 50 degrees, knee angle 64 degrees at the bottom of the rep.

findings.rule: Bar path — bar stays over the midfoot
findings.source_quote: good technique in barbell training is easily and understandably defined as the ability of the lifter to keep the bar vertically aligned with the balance point
findings.feedback: Bar drifted 53 px horizontally from the midfoot, measured on 277 of 277 frames (the plausible range of that figure is 27 to 80 px, because the bar and the midfoot are far apart vertically). The document states that any horizontal component of bar motion is not work against gravity (reference p11) and that flopping forward lets the bar drop forward of the midfoot (reference p33).
findings.uncertainty: Threshold {'tolerance_px': 25, 'min_samples': 3, 'min_sample_fraction': 0.2} is an application assumption; the document states the criterion qualitatively (reference p8, p9, p11, p33).

findings.rule: Bar placement — low bar, just below the scapular spine
findings.source_quote: The bar should therefore be in the lowest secure position it can occupy on the back, right below the spine of the scapula
findings.feedback: Bar height is consistent with the low-bar position described in the document. This is an estimate: confirming that the bar sits just under the spine of the scapula requires a rear view (references p29, p30).

findings.rule: Hip drive — hips go up, not forward
findings.source_quote: come up out of the bottom by driving your butt straight up in the air. Up, not forward.
findings.feedback: Hips drove up out of the bottom rather than forward, matching the document's 'up, not forward' instruction (reference p23).

findings.rule: Knee position — knees just forward of the toes
findings.source_quote: the knees are just a little forward of the toes
findings.feedback: Knees sit -6 px forward of the toe line, consistent with the bottom position the document describes (reference p22).
Hips are back over the heels at the bottom, as the document's bottom position describes (reference p22).

findings.source_quote: look down at a point on the floor 4-5 feet in front of you
findings.feedback: Head is pitched 7 degrees upward. The document is explicit that failing to look down kills hip drive, and that an upward gaze puts the cervical spine in an unsafe position under load (references p24, p26, p35).
findings.uncertainty: Threshold {'min_deg': 10} is an application assumption; the document states the criterion qualitatively (reference p24, p26, p35).

findings.rule: Stance width — heels about shoulder width
findings.feedback: Stance width is not observable in a side view; a front or rear view is required.
findings.uncertainty: Requires a front or rear view.

findings.source_quote: toes pointed out at about 30 degrees
findings.feedback: Toe angle is not observable in a side view; a front or rear view is required.
findings.uncertainty: Requires a front or rear view.

findings.rule: Knees tracking parallel to the feet (no valgus)
findings.source_quote: the knees are shoved out so that the thighs stay parallel to the feet
findings.feedback: Medial-lateral knee position is not observable in a side view; a front or rear view is required.
findings.uncertainty: Requires a front or rear view.

findings.source_quote: 16-17 inches between the ends of the outside knurl, and 32 inches between the finger marks
findings.feedback: Grip width and wrist alignment are not reliably observable in a side view.
findings.uncertainty: Requires a front or rear view.

findings.source_quote: Set the rack height so that the bar in the rack is at about the level of your mid-sternum
findings.feedback: Rack height is a setup measurement, not observable during the squat itself.
findings.uncertainty: Requires a front or rear view.

uncertainty_notes: Threshold {'tolerance_px': 25, 'min_samples': 3, 'min_sample_fraction': 0.2} is an application assumption; the document states the criterion qualitatively (reference p8, p9, p11, p33).
Threshold {'min_deg': 10} is an application assumption; the document states the criterion qualitatively (reference p24, p26, p35).
Requires a front or rear view.
